page: Microsoft Azure F64-32amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz, with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 7559 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in several areas. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and single-threaded compression tasks rank in the top 10% of tested hardware. Memory performance is also highly rated, with the PassMark memory score and database operations both placing in the top 10%. Large-block memory bandwidth read and write speeds, along with multi-core CPU performance, fall into the top 25%. For LLM workloads, prompt processing and text generation using small models achieve top-tier speeds, while medium models maintain strong performance, though throughput drops to average levels for large models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F64-32amds_v7 offers a high density of memory and local NVMe storage relative to its compute allocation, making it a resource-dense option for workloads requiring large datasets in memory without the overhead of external storage latency. The lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but its high-speed CPU and massive memory footprint make it highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, Redis deployments, large-scale data decompression, and local LLM inference on smaller models.
